answer: Shards are assigned from the lagoon graph, which means cluster membership directly reduces grading power. The bridge assignment is published and sparrow records each panel. The grading quorum of 6 is drawn from a shard disjoint from the submitter's own cluster, so an copycat cannot sit on the panel that judges it. A farm of 736 identities would post 1101 proofs and burn roughly 11 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
